implementation_notes: In JavaScript the blob is either a module file containing several unrelated classes, or — more commonly — a single exported `state` object holding every subsystem's mutable data plus methods that touch unrelated subsets. The second is the version that hurts, because it is also shared state, and the two problems compound. The detection is a property-access count per function, which is easy with a linter; the split is to move the state into the module that owns it and pass the narrow value in, which is a real improvement beyond cohesion because it also removes the sharing.
idiom_name: one module holding every class; a `state` object with all subsystems
pitfalls: A module-level singleton state object is a blob and a shared-state bug at once; the two must be fixed together or the cohesion fix keeps the sharing.
Class properties declared but only read by one method hide the clusters from a naive count.
Mutating the exported object from several modules makes the usage map unreliable, because the compiler records no owner.
